chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who forgets the opening Takbir. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat.'

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةَ الِافْتِتَاحِ: The opening Takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar') at the start of prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets the opening Takbir during prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that forgetting the opening Takbir is a minor omission that does not invalidate the prayer, requiring only its repetition. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (*yusr*) in worship, distinguishing between essential pillars (*arkan*) and recommended acts (*sunan*) that, when missed, do not nullify the ritual. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of key narrators like Jurij and Zura'ah, reinforcing the authenticity of this practical legal guidance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim Bin Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the man who forgets the exclamation of Takbīr in the beginning. Heasws said: ‘He should repeat’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah who has said the following: “
I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about one who forgets the opening Takbir (Allah is great beyond description). He (the Imam) said, ‘He says it again.’”
